newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mixed ahead of expiry, oil lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mixed ahead of expiry, oil lower.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended mixed on Monday with July posting strong gains on short covering ahead of Tuesday's expiry, pit sources said.
Soyoil ended lower after notching contracts lows in new crop months as rains fell in key growing areas of Illinois, easing concerns of heat and moisture stress.

"You started out with the weather, but after that the key factor was this July meal just won't give up," said Dave Armstrong, analyst with ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp. "There are no deliveries, no selling. The July meal kept coming back, the spread kept widening and that pulled everything back up."

There have been no deliveries posted against the July and none are expected as cash prices continue to trade at a premium to futures. Cash dealers began quoting basis against the August on Monday and most carried the full spread.

Open interest in the July was at 2,364 lots as of Friday's close, down 711 from the previous session, CBOT reported. Some trade sources said the open interest needed to fall further to ensure a quiet expiration on Tuesday.
Soymeal ended $5.00 per ton higher to $2.00 lower with July up $5.00 at $275.00. Soyoil closed down 0.38 to 0.29 cent per lb with December down 0.37 at 22.29.
Soyoil and new crop soymeal were pressured by weekend rains in dry pockets of central Illinois and forecasts for more moisture. The rains alleviated concerns of heat and moisture stress.

But some traders said the damage had already been done. After the close of trade, USDA said 62 percent of the U.S. soybean crop was rated good to excellent as of Sunday, down from 66 percent the previous week.

Forecasts called for 0.50 to 1.50 inches of rain in central Illinois through Tuesday with 60 to 80 percent coverage. Recent rains had bypassed central Illinois, leaving some fields in dire need of moisture.

On the day, commercials were light buyers of soymeal. ADM and Cargill Inc each bought 200 lots August, Central Soya bought 100 July and Term Commodities bought 200 December, traders said. Refco Inc bought 2200 each August and December and sold 100 August.
In soyoil, ADM bought 200 August and 100 September but sold 100 August. Cargill Inc and Term Commodities were also light buyers. Smith Barney and Refco Inc each sold 200 December.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 21,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 23,043 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 15,000 lots, against Friday's 16,830.
